_note: In-engine cinematics (play/cinematic.js; docs/PURSUIT.md). Each one: seconds long; who's in it and how they move (driven by the AI along the real road — the player's car on the quest's route, the police after it); and its shots, one after another. A shot: from–to (s), ease (linear, in, out, inOut), subject (whose car the camera is placed round: player, police — the first police car — or player:N, the Nth car of a party), path: the camera's control points [right, up, forward] in m from the subject (a smooth curve through them, from the first at the shot's start to the last at its end; "chase": the game's own chase camera at that moment — a shot ending on it hands over without a cut), look: where it looks [right, up, forward] from the subject (or "chase"), fov: [start, end] in degrees ("chase": the game's). player: the car's speed when it's let go (startKmh) and its throttle over time ([s, 0–1] pairs, eased between); police: when they pull out (pullOutAt), and how far behind they keep — gap at the start and at the handover (m). skip: where everyone is put when it's skipped (metres on from the start along the route, the speed: km/h; the police gapAtHandover behind).

pursuit_intro_coop._note: A party's: it plays through the race room's countdown — from GO − seconds to GO on the server's clock, the same moment on every game (data/multiplayer.json race.countdownSec: no longer than that) — all the party's cars in it, each driven by its own game's AI, the police car the host's.
